categories.name: It works
categories.notes: Build 5/5: 0 errors, and the 10 warnings are the scaffold's ImageSharp NuGet advisories, none introduced. Front page 10/10: / returns 200 and is the 'MCP Notes' blog front page, listing both posts as cards with a GetCropUrl image, date, title, excerpt and 'Read the post' link, all of which work. Posts 10/10: both posts render all 5 blocks (rich text, image, rich text, rich text, quote) with no render errors. Images 5/5: 6 of the provided Unsplash photos were imported into a 'Blog Images' media folder and served through signed GetCropUrl URLs; 6/6 load. Domain/publish 5/5: domain '/' on the Blog page, and all content is published.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: Folders 8/8: richTextBlock, imageBlock and quoteBlock are elements in Blocks; blogFrontPage and blogPost are documents in Pages. Block grid 7/7: 'Blog Block Grid' (Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid) allows the three blocks and is the body on both page types; the post blocks have sensible properties (text; image + caption; quote + attribution). Structure 4/5: siteRoot is the only root type, siteRoot→blogFrontPage→blogPost, templates are assigned, and aliases are camelCase. But siteRoot was also given blogFrontPage as allowed and default template, which is wrong for the template-less WWW container (the other mcp-recipe runs left it empty). Hygiene 5/5: no compositions; publishDate, excerpt and listingImage are real properties; nothing duplicated or orphaned.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: Pipeline 7/7: both page templates call Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "body"), with no custom loops, and the scaffold's grid partials are unchanged. Adapters 6/6: one markup-free adapter per block at blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml, each taking BlockGridItem<T>, mapping to a plain model (image URL built with GetCropUrl in the adapter) and calling Component.InvokeAsync. The RichTextBlockModel name collides with Umbraco's own, so it is fully qualified in the adapter, which is fine. ViewComponents 5.5/7: one per block (RichText, Image, Quote), rendering Default.cshtml, with plain models in Models/Blocks/. But all three component views use '@inherits UmbracoViewPage<TModel>' instead of '@model', so they still depend on Umbraco (code.componentViewsArePlain FAIL). Conventions 5/5: Program.cs and appsettings.json untouched, no migrations, no .cs in the Models/ root, friendly extensions and GetCropUrl, no injected services, and Tailwind built to wwwroot/dist/site.css.

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Posts 4.5/6: 'Why MCP Is Awesome' and 'One Protocol, Every Tool' (~300 words of body each, 6 paragraphs) are on topic and accurate: one contract instead of bespoke integrations, portability, scoping/permissions, an auditable log, and fast server development. Each is spread over 5 blocks with relevant credited photos (network lines, code on screen, puzzle hands). However, the posts are fairly generic, have no subheadings, use two rich text blocks back to back, and have invented quote attributions ('Priya, platform lead'). Looks 4/4: a clean, coherent Tailwind blog with a header and intro, a 'Latest posts' listing with image cards, readable post pages with a hero image, captions, a styled blockquote, back links and a footer.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Channel/order 2.5/3: all schema, media and the domain went through the umbraco MCP server, and pages, blocks and publishing through umbraco-editor (59 calls). The recipe's order was followed: model → media → content → publish → domain → stop/build → Razor → npm build → build/restart → curl checks. There was no DB, Management API, uSync or memory use, and no reads of results/ or tests/. Small deduction for a 'curl -o /tmp_page.html' that tried to write outside the project; it failed, and a stray page.tmp was removed. Report 2/2: accurate, and it discloses the flaky media import, the CS0104 fix and the /tmp slip.

summary: A complete, working MCP-built blog: three-block grid (rich text, image, quote), a front page listing two image cards, and two on-topic posts of 5 blocks each, rendered through the exact adapter → ViewComponent pipeline with a clean Tailwind design. The only flaws are component views that inherit UmbracoViewPage, a blogFrontPage template assigned to siteRoot, and somewhat generic post copy.
strengths: Everything works: build clean, /, both posts and all 6 images return 200, with no render errors
Textbook rendering pipeline: GetBlockGridHtmlAsync, markup-free alias-named adapters, one ViewComponent per block, plain models in Models/Blocks
Image URLs built with GetCropUrl in the adapter, so the component models carry only strings
Clean, coherent Tailwind design for both the listing and the post pages
Followed the recipe's order exactly through the two MCP servers, with an accurate, candid final report

issues.text: Component views use '@inherits UmbracoViewPage<TModel>' instead of '@model', which keeps an Umbraco dependency (Views/Shared/Components/{Image,Quote,RichText}/Default.cshtml)
siteRoot document type given blogFrontPage as allowed and default template; the WWW container should have none
Posts are fairly generic (~300 words each), with no subheadings, back-to-back rich text blocks and invented quote attributions (/why-mcp-is-awesome/, /one-protocol-every-tool/)
Stray 'curl -o /tmp_page.html' tried to write outside the project folder (failed; disclosed)
